The '''maximum agreement subtree problem''' is any of several closely related problems in [[graph theory]] and [[computer science]]. In all of these problems one is given a collection of [[Tree (graph theory)|trees]] <math>T_1,\ldots, T_m</math> each containing <math>n</math> leaves. The leaves of these trees are given labels from some set <math>L</math> with <math>|L|=n</math> so that no pair of leaves in the same tree sharing the same label, within the same tree the labelling for each leaf is distinct. In this problem one would like to find the largest subset <math>L'\subset L</math> such that the [[Minimum spanning tree|minimal spanning subtrees]] containing the leaves in <math>L'</math>,  of <math>T_1\mid S,\ldots, T_m\mid S</math> are the "same" while preserving the labelling.

== Formulations ==

===Maximum homeomorphic agreement subtree===
Source:<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Amir|first=A.|last2=Keselman|first2=D.|date=1997-12-01|title=Maximum Agreement Subtree in a Set of Evolutionary Trees: Metrics and Efficient Algorithms|journal=SIAM Journal on Computing|volume=26|issue=6|pages=1656–1669|doi=10.1137/S0097539794269461|issn=0097-5397|citeseerx=10.1.1.133.6891}}</ref>

This version requires that the subtrees <math>T_1\mid S,\ldots, T_m\mid S</math> are [[Homeomorphism (graph theory)|homeomorphic]] to one another.

====Rooted maximum homeomorphic agreement subtree====
This version is the same as the ''maximum homeomorphic agreement subtree'', but we further assume that <math>T_1,\ldots,T_m</math> are rooted and that the subtrees <math>T_1\mid S,\ldots, T_m\mid S</math> contain the root node. This version of the maximum agreement subtree problem is used for the study of [[phylogenetic trees]].<ref name=":0" /> Because of its close ties with phylogeny this formulation is often what is mean when one refers to the "maximum agreement subtree" problem.

=== Other variants ===
There exits other formulations for example the ''(rooted) maximum isomorphic agreement subtree''<ref name=":0" /> where we require the subtrees to be [[Graph isomorphism|isomorphic]] to one another.
